[head=2][color=#e8b04b]Melee Combat[/color][/head]
Melee on Hullrot: Eclipsion is not a simple click-fest. Swings, parries, stamina and positioning all matter, and a skilled fighter with a blade can beat a panicking one with a gun. This page explains how to actually win a melee fight.
[color=#d9776c]Turn on Combat Mode from your action bar before attacking or parrying.[/color]
[head=3][color=#e8b04b]The three attacks[/color][/head]
- [color=#6ab7d6][keybind="Use"/][/color] is your [bold]wide, committed attack[/bold]. It sweeps an arc and hits everything in it, allies included, so aim it at an enemy or object and allow room for the swing. - [color=#6ab7d6][keybind="UseSecondary"/][/color] is your [bold]parry or block[/bold]. It raises your guard to catch an incoming attack, and timing is everything. - [color=#6ab7d6][keybind="MouseMiddle"/][/color] is a [bold]light attack[/bold]. It strikes one target instead of sweeping an arc, so it will not catch an ally standing beside your enemy, but it can only be used about once every two seconds. Bare fists always swing light, so this is only for a weapon in hand.
[head=3][color=#e8b04b]Parrying, blocking, and the riposte[/color][/head]
You need a [bold]melee weapon in hand[/bold] to parry. Bare fists cannot, and neither can a gun.
Your guard stays up for about half a second, and the [bold]first fifth of a second[/bold] of that is the perfect window. Which one you get decides the whole exchange:
- A [color=#8fc98a]perfect parry[/color] takes no damage, gives you stamina back, staggers and slows the attacker, and opens a [bold]riposte[/bold]. Hit them within the next second or so and that strike lands for [color=#8fc98a]more than double damage[/color]. A popup tells you when the window is open. - An ordinary [color=#6ab7d6]block[/color] still stops the damage and staggers them briefly, but it costs you a little stamina and earns no riposte. - A [color=#d9776c]missed parry[/color] costs stamina and leaves you unable to parry again for a moment.
A perfect parry also requires you to be [bold]facing the attacker[/bold]. Turn into the blow, not away from it.
Watch your opponent's swings and learn their rhythm. Parry [bold]reactively[/bold] rather than on a loop. Against several attackers only one blow can be caught at a time, so try not to let yourself get surrounded.
[head=3][color=#e8b04b]Stamina[/color][/head]
Every committed swing spends [color=#e8b04b]stamina[/color], and landing it gives roughly that much back. [color=#d9776c]Missing is what drains you[/color], not attacking.
- Swinging wildly at empty air is the fastest way to run dry and lose your guard. - Blocks cost a little, failed parries cost more, and a perfect parry pays you back. - Draining [bold]your opponent's[/bold] stamina is a win condition. Make them swing and miss, then punish the stagger.
[head=3][color=#e8b04b]Wielding melee weapons[/color][/head]
Larger weapons like the zweihander and other heavy blades are far more effective when wielded in [bold]two hands[/bold]. Press [color=#6ab7d6][keybind="ActivateItemInHand"/][/color] while holding one to wield it. You need a free hand, so you cannot wield a weapon and hold a shield or gun at the same time.
Lighter weapons such as kukris, batons, and daggers can be used one-handed, letting you keep a sidearm or shield ready.
[head=3][color=#e8b04b]Executions[/color][/head]
You cannot instantly execute an active enemy. The target must first be incapacitated through normal combat.
With the weapon in your hand, press [color=#6ab7d6][keybind="UIRightClick"/][/color] on the incapacitated target to open the context menu, right click the entry again to open its verb menu, and select [bold]Execute[/bold]. Executions run on a do-after, so anything that interrupts you cancels it.
[color=#d9776c]Remember the rules.[/color] Executing a downed enemy is [color=#8fc98a]allowed[/color] during active combat between factions, but round-removing a member of your [bold]own faction[/bold] is forbidden. See the [textlink="Roleplay Rules" link="RoleplayRules"] for details.
[head=3][color=#e8b04b]Practical tips[/color][/head]
- Keep moving. A stationary target is easy to shoot and easy to surround. - Use doorways and corners to fight enemies one at a time instead of all at once. - A shield in your off-hand can soak hits while you swing with the other. - Do not bring a knife to a gunfight in the open. Close the distance through cover first. - Watch your stamina bar as closely as your health.
